question.problem:
Given that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{64}∼N(-14,{16}^{2})$ is a random sample of size $64$ from a normal population, calculate $P(\overset{―}{X}>-14.86).$

*Hint: A value table of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.5\,$ | $\,0.3015\,$ | $\,0.2981\,$ | $\,0.2946\,$ |
| $\,-0.4\,$ | $\,0.3372\,$ | $\,0.3336\,$ | $\,0.3300\,$ |
| $\,-0.3\,$ | $\,0.3745\,$ | $\,0.3707\,$ | $\,0.3669\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(-14,\frac{{16}^{2}}{64}) \\  & ∼N(-14,4).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(\overset{―}{X}>-14.86).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>-14.86) & =P(Z>\frac{-14.86-(-14)}{\sqrt{4}}) \\  & =P(Z>-0.43).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the complement of the normal distribution, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z>-0.43) & =1-P(Z\le -0.43) \\  & =1-Φ(-0.43).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.43)=0.3336.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>-14.86) & =1-Φ(-0.43) \\  & =1-0.3336 \\  & =0.6664.\end{aligned}
$$
